newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan faces rebellion at Fed, magazine says.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan faces rebellion at Fed, magazine says.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan faces a "mini-rebellion" at the central bank from anti-inflation hawks who want to increase interest rates, Business Week magazine reported in its latest edition.
"There is a division inside the Fed's hushed hallways over whether to raise interest rates," the magazine said.

On the one side are Greenspan and his fellow members of the Fed Board, who have resisted a rate hike. On the other are most of the 12 regional Fed bank presidents, who are pushing for tighter credit, according to the magazine.
The dispute revolves around a basic question, Business Week said -- does today's economy operate differently?

Greenspan and Fed Vice Chair Alice Rivlin believe it does and argue that heavy corporate investment in computers is boosting productivity far above its measured rate. The anti-inflation hawks disagree, Business Week said.

"Fed watchers bet that, absent signs of a slowdown, Greenspan will okay a quarter-point hike in the federal funds rate (at the next central bank policy-mkaing meeting on September 24)," the magazine added.
